_comment: Blog content registry. /blog/index.html and every /blog/{genres,artists,songs,trending,on-this-day}/index.html archive page read this file and render automatically. To publish a new article: place its page, then add one entry here. No markup changes required. type must be one of: genre-hub, artist-bio, song-story, trending, on-this-day. genre is the matching slug from genres.json, or null when the content isn't tied to one genre.

posts.title: British Invasion: How 1960s British Rock Bands Conquered America
posts.description: How UK bands led by The Beatles conquered American radio, charts, and TV starting in 1964, and the sound and artists that defined the movement.

posts.title: The Beatles: The Liverpool Band That Changed Music Forever
posts.description: How four teenagers from Liverpool became the most influential band in music history, from Hamburg's clubs to the studio innovations of Revolver and Sgt. Pepper.

posts.title: She Loves You: Inside The Beatles' Breakthrough 1963 Single
posts.description: How The Beatles wrote their biggest UK single on a tour bus, recorded it in a single day, and built pop's most famous closing chord in 1963.

posts.title: I Want to Hold Your Hand: How The Beatles Broke America
posts.description: How The Beatles wrote it eyeball to eyeball, then rode it to their first US number one and a nation-changing Ed Sullivan debut.

posts.title: Please Please Me: The Beatles' First UK Number One
posts.description: How John Lennon's Roy Orbison homage became The Beatles' first chart-topping single after George Martin sped up its tempo in one session.

posts.title: Brian Jones Rolling Stones: The Founder Behind the Band
posts.description: How a 20-year-old blues fanatic built the Rolling Stones, named it after Muddy Waters, and lost it before his death in 1969.

posts.title: (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction: Written in His Sleep
posts.description: How Keith Richards wrote the riff half asleep in a Florida motel room and turned it into the Stones' first US number one.

posts.title: Paint It Black Stones: The Hit Born From a Studio Joke
posts.description: How a joke on the organ and Brian Jones's brand-new sitar turned into the first sitar song ever to hit number one in the US and UK.

posts.title: The Kinks: How Getting Banned From America Changed Them
posts.description: How a slashed amp, a bloody onstage fight, and a four-year US touring ban turned Ray Davies into one of rock's most English songwriters.

posts.title: You Really Got Me: The Take Ray Davies Refused
posts.description: How Ray Davies refused to release the first take, forced a re-record at his own label's expense, and built a blueprint for hard rock.

posts.title: All Day and All of the Night: The Riff The Doors Copied
posts.description: How The Kinks doubled down on their own riff formula, then won a royalties fight when The Doors borrowed it too closely.

posts.title: Kinks Sunny Afternoon: Written During a Real Breakdown
posts.description: How Ray Davies wrote a breezy tax satire while recovering from a real nervous breakdown, then knocked The Beatles off number one.

posts.title: On This Day: September 1 in 1960s Music
posts.description: 21 verified 1960s music events from September 1: chart hits, festival closings, Beatles history, and notable births, each dated and sourced.
